tragicus.definition: tragicus adj. , tragiko/s, of tragedy, tragic: Carmen, i. e. tragedy, H.: Versūs, H.: actor, a tragedian, L.: Orestes aut Athamas, represented in tragedy: cerva, i. e. in the tragedy of Iphigenia, Iu.— As subst m., a …

tragoedia.definition: tragoedia ae, f , tragw|di/a, a tragedy: tragoedias fecit.—Tragedy, the art of tragedy: Paulum Musa Tragoediae Desit theatris, H.: Omne genus scripti gravitate tragoedia vincit, O.— Person.: ingenti Tragoedia passu, O…

tragoedus.definition: tragoedus ī, m , tragw|do/s, a tragic actor, tragedian, C., H.

tragula.definition: trāgula ae, f TRAG-, a javelin thrown by a strap, hand-dart : femur tragulā traicitur, Cs.: tragulā graviter ictus, L.

tragus.definition: tragus ī, m , tra/gos, a kind of fish, O.

trahea.definition: trahea ae, f TRAG-, a drag, sledge , V.

traho.definition: trahō trāxī (inf perf. trāxe for trā xisse, V.), tractus, ere TRAG-, to draw, drag, haul, train along, draw off, pull forth, drag away : cum a custodibus in fugā trinis catenis vinctus traheretur, Cs.: trahantur pedib…

traicio.definition: trāiciō (trāiic-) and trānsiciō (trānsiic-), iēcī, iectus, ere trans + iacio, to throw across, cause to cross, cause to go across, put over, transfer, throw over, shoot across : neque ullum interim telum traiciebatur,…

traiectio.definition: trāiectiō ōnis, f trans+IA-, a crossing over, passing over, passage : honestior existimatur traiectio: traiectiones motūsque stellarum, i. e. shooting-stars .—Fig., of language, a transposition : verborum.— Exaggerati…

traiectus2.definition: trāiectus (trānsie-) ūs, m trans+IA-, a crossing over, passing over, passage : in Britanniam, Cs.: in traiectu Albulae amnis submersus, L.

trames.definition: trāmes itis, m 1 TER-, a cross-way, side-way, by-path, foot-path : egressus est tramitibus paludatus: per tramites occulte perfugere, S.: transvorsis tramitibus transgressus, L.: silvae, V.— Poet., a way, path, road, …

tranato.definition: trānatō (trānsn-) —, —, āre, to swim across, pass beyond: Gangen.

trano.definition: trānō (trānsnō) āvī, — , āre trans+no, to swim over, swim across, swim through : in Tiberim desiluit et ad suos tranavit, L.: flumen, Cs.: paludem, Cu.: Obsequio tranantur aquae, O.— To go through, pass through, penet…

tranquille.definition: tranquillē adv. tranquillus, calmly, quietly, tranquilly : tranquille placideque: dicere.

tranquillitas.definition: tranquillitās ātis, f tranquillus, quietness, stillness, tranquillity, calmness, calm : tanta tranquillitas exstitit, ut se ex loco commovere non possent (naves), Cs.: mira serenitas cum tranquillitate oriebatur, L.: …

tranquillo1.definition: tranquillō adv. tranquillus, quietly, without disturbance : nec cetera modo tribuni tranquillo peregere, L.

tranquillo2.definition: tranquillō —, ātus, āre tranquillus, to make calm, calm, still, compose, tranquillize : animos: tranquillatis rebus Romanis, when order was restored at Rome , N.: Quid pure tranquillet, honos an dulce lucellum, H.

tranquillus.definition: tranquillus adj. with comp. and sup, quiet, calm, still, tranquil: mare, quod naturā suā tranquillum sit: tranquillo mari gubernare, L.: aquae, O.—As subst n., a quiet sea, calm: te ad scopulum e tranquillo auferre, T…

trans.definition: trāns praep. with acc. 1 TER-.—Of motion, across, over, to the farther side of : qui trans mare currunt, H.: multitudinem trans Rhenum traducere, Cs.: trans vallum signum traicere, L.: curvos trans ripam miserat arcū …

transabeo.definition: trāns-abeō iī, —, īre, to go through, pierce through, transfix: ensis Transabiit costas, V.

transactor.definition: trānsāctor ōris, m trans+1 AC-, a manager, conductor : rerum.

transadigo.definition: trāns-adigō ēgī, āctus, ere, to thrust through, drive through: costas ensem, V.—To pierce through: Horum unum ad medium . . . Transadigit costas, V.

transalpinus.definition: trāns-alpīnus adj., beyond the Alps, transalpine, Cs., C.

transcendo.definition: trānscendō dī, —, ere trans + scando, to climb over, pass over, cross, overstep, surmount : in hostium navīs, Cs.: in finīs hostium, L.: per Vescinos in Campaniam, L.: vallī s, Cs.: Alpīs.— Fig., to pass over, pass by…

transcribo.definition: trānscrībō (trans-scr-) īpsī , īptus, ere, to write over, transcribe, write anew, transfer in writing, alter, forge: testamentum in alias tabulas transcriptum: tabulas publicas.—To make over, transfer, assign, convey,…

transcurro.definition: trāns-currō currī or cucurrī, cursus, ere, to run over, run across, go by, pass: hinc ad forum, T.: praeter oculos, O.: remos transcurrentes detergere, in sailing by, Cs.: haud dubius, sine noxā transcursuros, si nemo…

transenna.definition: trānsenna ae, f a netting, lattice-work: quasi per transennam aspeximus.

transeo.definition: trāns-eō iī (rarely īvī; fut. trānsiet, Tb.; fut perf. trānsierītis, O.), itus, īre, to go over, go across, cross over, pass over, pass by, pass: ad uxorem meam, T.: e suis finibus in Helvetiorum finīs, Cs.: per media…

transfero.definition: trāns-ferō tulī, lātus (or trālā tus), ferre, to bear across, bring through, carry over, convey over, transport, transfer: Illinc huc transferri, T.: Naevius trans Alpīs usque transfertur: paulo ultra eum locum castra…

transfigo.definition: trāns-fīgō fīxī, fīxus, ere, to pierce through, transpierce, transfix: ea, quā erat transfixus, hasta: transfixi telis, Cs.: gladio puellam, L.: transfigitur scutum Pulioni, Cs.: unguibus anguem: transfixo pectore, V.…

transfodio.definition: trāns-fodiō fōdī, fossus, ere, to pierce through, run through, stab through, transfix, transpierce: Galli transfodiebantur, Cs.: fugienti latus, L.: pectora duro Transfossi ligno, V.

transformis.definition: trānsfōrmis e, adj. trans+forma, changed in shape, transformed : (Proteus) transformis, O.: corpora, O.

transformo.definition: trāns-fōrmō āvī, ātus, āre, to change in shape, transform, transfigure, metamorphose: Omnia sese in miracula rerum, V.: in torvos membra iuvencos, O.: gemmas novem in ignīs (i. e. stellas), O.

transfuga.definition: trānsfuga ae trans+2 FVG-, one who joins the enemy, a deserter : non omnia illum transfugam ausum esse senatui dicere: plebs, transfuga ex suis populis, L.: proditores et transfugas arboribus suspendunt, Ta.: transfug…

transfugio.definition: trāns-fugiō fūgī, —, ere, to flee to the other side, go over to the enemy, desert: Romam, L.: ad hostes, N.—Fig.: non ab adflictā amicitiā transfugere atque ad florentem aliam devolare.

transfugium.definition: trānsfugium ī, n trans+2 FVG-, a going over to the enemy, desertion , L.

transfundo.definition: trāns-fundō fūdī, —, ere, to pour off, transfer, turn, divert: omnīs meas laudes ad te: eorum mores in Macedonas, Cu.

transfusio.definition: trānsfūsiō ōnis, f trans+FV-, a decanting, intermingling .

transgredior.definition: trānsgredior gressus, ī, dep. trans+gradior, to step across, step over, climb over, pass over, cross : hunc Britanniae statum mediā iam aestate transgressus invenit, Ta.: in Corsicam, sail over , L.: flumen, cross , C…

transgressio.definition: trānsgressiō ōnis, f trans+GRAD-, a going across, going over, passing over, passage : Gallorum.—Fig., in rhet., a transposition : verborum.

transgressus2.definition: trānsgressus ūs, m trans+GRAD-, a passing over, passage, crossing auspicium prosperi transgressūs, Ta.: in transgressu amoris, Ta.

transigo.definition: trānsigō ēgī, āctus, ere trans+ago, to drive through, stab through, pierce through, transfix, transpierce : gladio pectus, Ph.—Fig., to carry through, bring to an end, finish, settle, complete, conclude, perform, acco…

transilio.definition: trānsiliō or trānssiliō uī , —, īre trans+ salio, to leap across, jump over, spring over, overleap : ex humilioribus in altiorem navem, L.: Per tantum terrae credere Iudicium studii transiluisse mei, i. e. to have ext…

transitio.definition: trānsitiō ōnis, f trans+1 I-, a going across, going over, passing over, passage : ut similitudine et transitione cernatur, i. e. by the passing by of atoms : visionum.— A going over, desertion : ad plebem transitiones…

transitus2.definition: trānsitus —, acc. um, abl. ū, m trans+ 1 I-, a going over, passing over, passage : fossae: Tencterorum, Cs.: per agros transitum dare, L.— A passing over, desertion : transitū s mora, Ta.— Fig., a passing over, passin…

translaticius.definition: trānslātīcius (trālātī cius) adj. translatus, handed down, transmitted, traditional, hereditary, customary : edictum, i. e. in accordance with precedent.—Usual, customary, common : loqui more <*>anslaticio, Ph.

translatio.definition: trānslātiō (trāl-) ōnis, f trans+TAL-, a carrying across, removal, transporting, transferring : pecuniarum a iustis dominis ad alienos.— Fig., a transferring, shifting, diversion : criminis: actio translationis indige…

translativus.definition: trānslātīvus adj. translatio, of transference, to be transferred, to be sifted : constitutio.

translator.definition: trānslātor ōris, m trans+TAL-, one who carries over, a transferrer : quaesturae, i. e. who, while quaestor, deserted to Sulla .

transluceo.definition: trāns-lūceō (trāl-) — , —, ēre, to shine through, glimmer through: In liquidis aquis, O.

transmarinus.definition: trāns-marīnus adj., beyond sea, from over the sea, transmarine: subsidium: artes: legationes, L.: doctrina, i. e. jurisprudence.

transmeans.definition: trānsmeāns ntīs, P. trans-meo, going over, going across , Ta.

transmigro.definition: trāns-migrō —, —, are, to remove, migrate, transmigrate: urbem, quo transmigremus, L.

transmissio.definition: trānsmissiō ōnis, f trans+MIT-, a sending across, passing over, passage : superior tua: ab eā urbe in Graeciam.

transmissus2.definition: trānsmissus (ūs), m trans+MIT-, a passing over, passage : ex Galliā in Britanniam, Cs.

transmitto.definition: trāns-mittō (trām-) mīsī, missus, ere, to send across, carry over, convey through, bring across, send off, despatch, transmit, let pass: exercitus equitatusque celeriter transmittitur (i. e. trans flumen), Cs.: cohort…

transmontanus.definition: trāns-montānus adj., beyond the mountains. — Plur. m. as subst, the people beyond the mountains, L.

transmoveo.definition: trāns-moveō —, —, ēre, to remove, transfer: gloriam Verbīs in sc. T.

transmuto.definition: trāns-mūtō āre, to change, shift, transmute: incertos honores, H.

transnato.definition: trāns-natō, trāns-nō see trā natō, trānō.

transpono.definition: trānspōnō posuī, —, ere, to set over, transfer: militem, Ta.

transporto.definition: trāns-portō āvī, ātus, āre, to carry over, take across, carry, convey, remove, transport: duas legiones, Cs.: ratibus equitem phalangemque, Cu.: in Macedoniam exercitum: exercitum in naves impositum in Hispaniam, L.: …

transrhenanus.definition: trāns-rhēnānus adj. Rhenus, beyond the Rhine , Cs.—Plur m . as subst, dwellers beyond the Rhine , Cs.

transtrum.definition: trānstrum ī, n 1 TER-, a cross-beam, crossbank, bank for rowers, thwart : transtra pedalibus trabibus confixa, Cs.: considite transtris, V.: transtra carinae, O.

transulto.definition: trānsultō (trānssu-) —, —, āre, freq. transsilio, to leap over, spring across : in recentem equum ex fesso, L.

transutus.definition: trānsūtus or trāns-sūtus P., stitched through, spitted: verubus transuta salignis Exta, O.

transveho.definition: trāns-vehō or trāvehō vē xī, vectus, ere, to carry across, convey over, bear to the other side, transport: quid militum transvexisset, Cs.: ut iam Hispanos omnes inflati travexerint utres, L.— Pass: legiones ex Sicili…

transverbero.definition: trāns-verberō —, —, āre, to strike through, thrust through, pierce through, transfix: bestia venabulo transverberatur: abiete pectus, V.

transversa.definition: trānsversa adv. Plur n. of transversus, across, askance, sideways : Mutati fremunt venti, V.

transversarius.definition: trānsversārius (trāvers-) adj. transversus, lying across, transverse : tigna, cross-beams , Cs.

transversus.definition: trāns-versus or trāversus (-vorsus) adj., turned across, lying across, thwart, crosswise, transverse: viae, cross-streets: tramites, L.: fossas transversas viis praeducit, Cs.: transverso ambulans foro, across the for…

transvolo.definition: trāns-volō (trāvolō) — , —, āre, to fly over, fly across, pass quickly over: in partem alteram, L.: Importunus (Cupido) transvolat aridas Quercūs (i. e. vetulas), H.—Fig.: Transvolat in medio posita, passes over, H.

trapetum.definition: trapētum ī, n trape/w , an olive-mill, oilmill : teritne baca trapetis, V.

trapezephorum.definition: trapezephorum (-zoph-) ī, n , trapezofo/ron, a pedestal, table-support, carved table-leg.

travectio.definition: trāvectiō (trānsv-) ōris, f trans+VAG-, a carrying across, crossing over : Acherontis.

traveho.definition: trāvehō, trāversārius, trāversus, trāvolō see transv-.

treceni.definition: trecēnī ae, a, num distr. tres+centum, three hundred each, three hundred : equites in singulis legionibus, L.: trecenis, quotquot eunt dies, placare Plutona tauris, three hecatombs a day , H.

trecentesimus.definition: trecentēsimus adj. trecenti, the three-hundredth : annus, L.

trecenti.definition: trecentī ae, a, num adj. tres+centum, three hundred : se trecentosque eos opposuit hostibus: iuvenes, V.: milia modium tritici, L.: amatorem trecentae cohibent catenae, i. e. innumerable , H.

trecenties.definition: trecentiēs adv. num. trecenti, three hundred times , Ct.

trechedipna.definition: trechedīpna orum, n , = * trexe/deipna (running to a feast), Greek slippers (worn by parasites), Iu.

tredecim.definition: tredecim num. tres+decem, thirteen : tredecim captis navibus, L.

tremebundus.definition: tremebundus (tremib-) adj. tremo, trembling, quivering, shaking : manus: Membra, O.

tremefacio.definition: tremefaciō fēcī, factus, ere tremo+facio, to cause to shake, agitate, make tremble : nutu Olympum, V.: se tremefecit tellus, quaked , C. poët.: tremefacta tellus, V.: scuticae habenis, O.

tremendus.definition: tremendus adj. P. of tremo, to be dreaded, fearful, dreadful, frightful, formidable, terrible, tremendous : rex, V.: oculi, O.: Alpes, H.: Carmentis monita, V.

tremesco.definition: tremēscō (tremīscō) —, —, ere, inch. tremo, to begin to shake, tremble, quake, dread : tonitru tremescunt Ardua terrarum, V.: iubeo tremescere montes, O.: sonitumque pedum vocem<*> que, V.: telum instare, V.

tremo.definition: tremō uī, —, ere 2 TER-, to shake, quake, quiver, tremble : totus Tremo horreoque, T.: toto pectore: corde et genibus, H.: tremis ossa pavore, H.: tremit artūs, V.: cum a me trementibus labris requirebas: cum tremeren…

tremor.definition: tremor ōris, m 2 TER-, a shaking, quaking, quivering, trembling, tremor : terrorem tremor consequatur: gelidus: donec manibus tremor incidat unctis, H.—Person.: Frigus iners illic habitant Pallorque Tremorque, O.— An …

tremulus.definition: tremulus adj. 2 TER-, shaking, quaking, quivering, trembling, tremulous : manus annisque metuque, O.: guttur, C. poët.: Ut mare fit tremulum, tenui cum stringitur aura, O.: flamma, V.

trepidanter.definition: (trepidanter) adv. trepido, tremblingly, with trepidation .—Only comp: trepidantius agere, Cs.

trepidatio.definition: trepidātiō ōnis, f trepido, confused hurry, alarm, agitation, confusion, consternation, trepidation : numquae trepidatio?: nec opinata res plus trepidationis fecit, quod, etc., L.: pilis inter primam trepidationem abi…

trepide.definition: trepidē adv. trepidus, in confusion, tremblingly, with trepidation : concursans, Ph.: classis soluta, L.: castra relinquere, L.

trepido.definition: trepidō āvī, ātus, āre trepidus.— Of persons, to hurry with alarm, be in confusion, be agitated, be disturbed : festinare, trepidare, S.: Quid est quod trepidas, T.: trepidante totā civitate ad excipiendum Poenum, L.:…

trepidus.definition: trepidus adj. TARC-, restless, agitated, anxious, solicitous, disturbed, alarmed, in trepidation : Tum trepidae inter se coëunt (apes), in a hurry , V.: inproviso metu, S.: formidine, V.: (apes) trepidae rerum discurr…

tres.definition: trēs (trīs) tria, gen. trium, acc. trēs or trīs, adj. num. cf. Gr. trei=s; Engl. three, three : trīs legatos deligere: horum trium generum quodvis: tria non commutabitis Verba inter vos, not three words , i. e. nothin…

tresviri.definition: trēs-virī or trēs virī or IIIvirī ōrum, m three associates in office, a board of three colleagues, three joint commissioners: tres viros epulones esse voluerunt, priests' assistants: tresviros creare consul iussus (to…

triangulus.definition: triangulus adj. tres+angulus, with three corners, three-cornered, triangular : sidera.—As subst n., a triangle : trianguli forma.

triarii.definition: triāriī ōrum, m tres, soldiers of the third rank in battle order, the reserve : ubi triarii consurrexerunt, integri, etc., L.—Prov.: rem ad triarios redisse, i. e. demanded extreme measures , L.

tribas.definition: tribas adis, f , triba/s, an abandoned woman, Ph.

tribolus.definition: tribolus (-bulus) ī, m , tribolos, a thorn bush, thistle, caltrop, V., O.

tribuarius.definition: tribuārius adj. tribus, of a tribe, of tribes : crimen, i. e. a bribing of the tribes : res.

tribulis.definition: tribūlis is, m tribus, a fellow tribesman : tuus: tribulibus enim iudicibus: conviva, H.

tribulum.definition: trībulum (trīvol-) ī, n 1 TER-, a threshingsledge, wooden platform studded with iron teeth , V.

tribunal.definition: tribūnal ālis, n tribunus, a raised platform for the seats of magistrates, judgment-seat, tribunal : praetoris: praetor tribunal suum iuxta praetoris sellam conlocavit, Cs.: quem ad se vocari et de tribunali citari iu…

tribunatus.definition: tribūnātus ūs, m tribunus, the office of a tribune, tribuneship : militaris, the office of a military tribune : qui eum vexandis consulibus permissurum tribunatum credebant, i. e. would give free scope to the tribunes…

tribunicius.definition: tribūnīcius adj. tribunus, of a tribune, tribunitial : potestas: vis, Cs.: seditiones, S.: procellae, L.: comitia, to elect tribunes of the people : leges, moved by the tribunes : honor, i. e. of military tribunes , C…

tribunus.definition: tribūnus ī, m tribus, the head of a tribe (see tribus); hence, a president, commander, representative, tribune : tribunus celerum, in quo tum magistratu forte Brutus erat, L.—Esp., tribuni aerarii, paymasters, quaesto…

tribuo.definition: tribuō uī, ūtus, ere tribus, to assign, impart, allot, bestow, confer, yield, give : ut ei plurimum tribuamus, a quo plurimum diligamur: si uni omnia tribuenda sint: cui magna Pompeius praemia tribuit, Cs.: Dona nulli…

tribus.definition: tribus ūs (dat. and abl plur., tribūbus, C., L.), f cf. tres, a third part of the people (as orig. divided into Ramnes, Tities, and Luceres); hence, in pen., an hereditary division of the people, tribe (under the cons…

tributarius.definition: tribūtārius adj. tributum, of tribute, relating to contributions : tabellae, i. e. promising rich gifts .

tributim.definition: tribūtim adv. tribus, through each tribe, tribe by tribe, by tribes : descriptis ordinibus: ut quod tributim plebes iussisset, populum teneret, i. e. in the comitia of the tribes , L.: adripuit populum tributim, H.

tributio.definition: tribūtiō ōnis, f tribuo, a distributing, distribution : aequabilis.

tributum.definition: tribūtum ī, n P. n. of tribuo, a stated payment, contribution, tribute : in capita singula servorum tributum imponebatur, Cs.: ex censu quotannis tributa conferre: civitates tributis liberare: tributo populo indicto, …

tributus2.definition: tribūtus adj. tribus, formed into tribes, marshalled by tribes : comitia, L.

tricae.definition: trīcae ārum, f TARC-, perplexities, subterfuges, quirks, wiles, tricks : domesticae.

triceni.definition: trīcēnī ae, a, num distr. triginta, thirty at a time, thirty each, thirty : lecti.

triceps.definition: trīceps cipitis, adj. tres+caput, with three heads, triple-headed : Cerberus.—Poet.: Hecate, of three forms (as also Luna and Diana), O.

tricesimus.definition: trīcēsimus or trīcēnsimus adj. num. triginta, the thirtieth : legio: tricensimo post die: sextus et tricesimus annus: tricesimum annum agens, L.: tricesimo die, Cu.

trichila.definition: trichila ae, f a summer-house, pavilion, bower, Cs. (al. triclinia).

triciens.definition: trīciēns or trīciēs num adv. triginta, thirty times : mea (filia) triciens (aeris millies) non posset (habere), i. e. three millions of sester<*> ces: HS triciens.

triclinium.definition: trīclīnium ī, n , trikli/nion, a couch for three persons reclining at meals, eating-couch, dinner-sofa, table-couch: rogatus est, ut triclinium sterneret.—An eating-room, dining-room, supperroom: alia fori vis est, al…

tricor.definition: trīcor ātus, ārī, dep. tricae, to make difficul ties, trifle, dally, shuffle, play tricks : tecum.

tricorpor.definition: (tricorpor) oris, adj. tres+corpus, with three bodies, of threefold form : forma tricorporis umbrae, i. e. of Geryon , V.

tricuspis.definition: (tricuspis, idis) adj. tres+cuspis, with three points, three-tined, tricuspid : posito tricuspide telo, i. e. the trident , O.

tridens.definition: tridēns entis (abl. dentī), adj. tres+dens, with three teeth, three-tined, three-pronged, tridented, trident : rostra, V.—As subst m . (abl. dentī or dente), a three-tined spear, trident : tellus percussa tridenti, V.…

tridentifer.definition: tridentifer ferī, m tridens+1 FER-, the trident-bearer (of Neptune), O.

tridentiger.definition: tridentiger gērī, m tridens + GES-, the trident-bearer (of Neptune), O.

triduum.definition: trīduum ī, n tres+dies; sc. spatium, three days' time, three days : biduist aut tridui Haec sollicitudo? T.: biduo post aut non toto triduo: triduo aut summum quatriduo periturus: triduo intermisso, Cs.

triennia.definition: triennia ium, n tres+annus; sc. sacra, a festival held every three years, triennial festival .

triennium.definition: triennium ī, n tres+annus; sc. spatium, three years' time, three years : triennium est, cum, etc.

triens.definition: triēns entis, m tres, a third part, third : cum sciemus, quantum quasi sit in trientis triente: cum duobus coheredibus esse in triente, i. e. be heir to one third of the estate .—As a coin, the third part of an as , H…

trientabulum.definition: trientābulum ī, n * triento, from triens, land assigned in commutation of one third of a public debt , L.

trierarchus.definition: triērarchus ī, m , trih/rarxos, a captain of a trireme, trierarch.

trieris.definition: triēris e, adj. , trih/rhs, with three banks of oars.—Only as subst f. (sc. navis), a galley with three banks of oars, trireme, N.
